title: CREATION
text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

body.kids: Everything that exists was made on purpose. Including you.
body.teens: The opening line argues for nothing and assumes everything: no rival gods, no conflict, no accident.

q.kids: What is the first thing the Bible says?
q.teens: What does Genesis 1:1 assume rather than argue?

why.teens: That God is there and creating — the text never argues the point.

title: THINGS GO WRONG
text: Yahweh God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”

body.kids: People chose their own way instead of God's. But God came looking.
body.teens: The first question after the fall is not an accusation. It is a search.

q.kids: What did God do after people disobeyed?
q.teens: What is God's first move after the fall?

why.kids: He came looking and called out.
why.teens: He seeks, and the question is pastoral before it is judicial.

title: A PEOPLE AND A PROMISE
text: In you all the families of the earth will be blessed.

body.kids: God promised Abraham a family, a land, and a blessing for everyone on earth.
body.teens: The promise is universal from the start — one family chosen for the sake of all the others.

q.teens: How wide is the Abrahamic promise?

why.kids: All the families of the earth.
why.teens: Universal in scope, though particular in method.

title: JESUS
text: The Word became flesh and lived among us.

body.kids: God did not stay far away. He came and lived with us.
body.teens: ‘Lived among us’ is literally ‘pitched his tent’ — the tabernacle word. John locates the incarnation in Israel's story.

q.teens: What does John's tabernacle language do?

options: God came and lived with us

why.kids: God came to live with people.
why.teens: It places the incarnation inside Israel's worship history rather than Greek metaphysics.

title: THE CHURCH
text: They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other languages.

body.kids: God's Spirit came, and ordinary people started telling everyone about Jesus — in every language in the city.
body.teens: Acts 2 reverses Babel: there language scattered people, here languages gather them.

q.teens: How does Acts 2 relate to Babel?

options: People heard in their own languages

why.kids: Everyone heard about Jesus in their own language.
why.teens: It reverses it — scattering becomes gathering.
